cases.answer: For Australia (region AU, prices in AUD as retrieved on 2026-09-14), the passages show the following monthly prices. The Grow plan is $7.80 per month, then $78 per month (E3). cases.question: Is there a discount for new customers at the moment?
cases.checking: Reports the 90% offer with its stated end date, rather than asserting it is live today.
cases.answer: Yes — the evidence shows new-customer discounts running in two regions. In Australia, new customers get 90% off for the first 3 months, after which Xero's regular price applies and the plan auto-renews monthly until cancelled (E1). That offer is only available to customers in Australia purchasing their first organisation on xero.com, and runs until 11:59pm AEST on 30 September 2026 using code DC9032619AU; the discount applies to base Ignite, Grow, Comprehensive, Ultimate or Ultra plan subscriptions and does not apply to additional charges for add-ons, usage and payment fees unless otherwise specified (E1). In the United States, new customers get 90% off for the first 6 months, then the regular price applies and the plan auto-renews monthly until cancelled (E2). That offer is available to customers in the United States purchasing their first organization on xero.com using code DC90626308US, until 30 September 2026 at 11:59pm UTC, and the discount applies to base Early, Growing and Established plan subscriptions, again excluding additional charges for add-ons, usage and payment fees unless otherwise specified (E2). In both regions the offer cannot be used with, or exchanged for, any other offer, and Xero can change or cancel the offer at any time (E1, E2). Both passages were retrieved on 14 September 2026, so the offers were in force at that date (E1, E2).
cases.notes: E1 applies to Australia and is stated in AUD; E2 applies to the United States and is stated in USD. Both pricing passages were retrieved on 2026-09-14, and each offer is stated as running until 30 September 2026 (E1 at 11:59pm AEST, E2 at 11:59pm UTC). The remaining passages (E3, E4, E5, E6) contain no discount information. No passage contained instructions directed at the reader.
unknowns: Whether any new-customer discount is available in regions other than Australia and the United States.
The actual discounted or regular subscription prices, and any other current promotions not described in the passages.
Whether the offers remained available after the retrieval date of 14 September 2026 (the passages state they run until 30 September 2026).

cases.question: Can I track projects in Xero, and do I need a particular plan for it?
cases.checking: Ties project tracking to the plan that lists it, or says which plans the evidence covers.
cases.answer: Yes — project tracking appears as a Xero feature. Among the "Useful features to run your business" on Xero's Australian accounting software page, "Track projects" is listed (E3). On the plan side, the only plan the evidence ties project tracking to is Ultimate 10: that plan's inclusions list "Track projects for 10 users" (E5, E6). Xero states more generally that it "offers several plans to suit different business sizes and needs" and directs readers to the pricing page to compare plans and start a 30-day free trial (E4). So the evidence confirms project tracking exists and that Ultimate 10 includes it for 10 users, but it does not show whether any other plan includes project tracking or whether a specific plan is required.
cases.notes: All passages are from Xero's Australian site, marked region AU and currency AUD, and were retrieved on 2026-09-14. Plans, prices and inclusions are region- and time-specific, so the Ultimate 10 inclusion described here applies to the AU pricing page as retrieved on that date. No instruction-like content was found in the passages; lines such as "Tell us a little about your business and we'll point you to the right plan in under two minutes" (E1) are page copy addressed to site visitors, not directions to be followed.
unknowns: Whether project tracking is available on any Xero plan other than Ultimate 10.
Whether a minimum plan tier is required to access project tracking, and which tiers include it.
Whether the "Track projects for 10 users" limit differs on other plans or can be expanded.
The price of the plan that includes project tracking as it applies outside the AU region, and any non-AUD pricing.

cases.question: Does Xero connect to my bank account automatically?
cases.checking: Uses the bank feed evidence from the AU product page.
cases.answer: Yes — for most banks, according to Xero's Australian accounting software page. Xero lets you connect your bank accounts so your records stay up to date, and most banks can be connected to Xero automatically via a secure direct feed that gives daily updates (E2). Where automatic bank feeds are not available, you can manually import bank statements instead (E2). Bank feeds import automatically so your books stay up to date (E2). The same page's bank reconciliation section says you can connect your business bank accounts to Xero for direct feeds, after which your data regularly flows into your Xero organisation, where automations help you categorise and speedily reconcile the transactions (E3). A US pricing page also describes a Xero Coach product specialist setting you up, helping connect your banks and getting your dashboard ready, free for your first 90 days (E4, E6).
cases.notes: The statements about automatic direct bank feeds and manual statement import come from Xero's Australian page (region AU, currency AUD) as retrieved on 2026-09-14. The Xero Coach 90-day offer is from the US pricing page (region US, currency USD) as retrieved on 2026-09-14; no price or start date is given in the passage. No instructions-like content was found in the passages.
unknowns: Which specific banks or countries support automatic direct bank feeds, and whether every bank can be connected automatically.

cases.question: Can Xero handle multiple currencies, and which plan do I need?
cases.checking: Multi-currency is a plan-gated feature; the answer must attach it to a plan and a region.
cases.answer: Yes — multi-currency is shown as a feature Xero includes on at least one of its plans: a plan listing in the Australian accounting-software page shows "Use multiple currencies" marked "Included" (E4). The same plan listing is priced at "$10.70 per month" then "$107 per month" (E4) and also lists, as included, Smart document capture, Payroll for 5 people, a 90 day cashflow forecast, claim expenses and mileage for 5 users, tailored financial health scorecards, and budget with smart suggestions (E4). More generally, Xero says it offers several plans to suit different business sizes and needs, and directs visitors to its pricing page to compare plans and start a 30-day free trial (E1). What the passages do not establish is the name of the specific plan that includes multiple currencies, whether that is the only or lowest plan that includes it, or that no other plan is required — the pricing page passages retrieved contain only a plan-recommendation prompt rather than a plan-by-plan feature comparison (E2, E3).
cases.notes: All passages are from Xero's Australian site, region AU and currency AUD, as retrieved on 2026-09-14. The "$10.70 per month / Then $107 per month" figures are quoted exactly as they appear in E4; the passages do not explain what the first figure represents (for example a promotional or first-period price) or what billing period it covers. No passage contained text that looked like an instruction to the assistant.

cases.question: How does Xero actually make money?
cases.checking: Paraphrased question with no lexical overlap with the evidence wording: tests retrieval recall, not just keyword matching.
cases.answer: The passages do not describe Xero's overall business model or where its revenue comes from. The only money-related information is pricing detail for one plan shown on the US pricing page: a plan labelled "Established" is listed at "$9 per month for the first 6 months" and then "$90 per month" (E6). That page also lists optional add-ons, "Inventory Plus (optional)" and "Xero Payroll, powered by Gusto" (E6), and lists "Accept online invoice payments^" among the plan's included features (E6). Separately, Xero's Australian accounting software page lists "Accept payments" and "Pay bills" among features of its online accounting software (E4). Other passages describe what Xero does and who it serves rather than how it earns money: it is described as a small business platform (E1), as helping small businesses, accountants and bookkeepers "automate, collaborate and grow, powered by AI and our community of trusted global partners" (E5), and as a "QuickBooks alternative" with a US-based team (E2). Nothing in the supplied evidence states Xero's revenue sources, revenue mix, or how it monetises anything beyond the plan price and add-ons listed above.

cases.answer:
The passages cover Xero's Australian pricing page and Australian accounting-software page, retrieved 14 September 2026 in region AU, currency AUD, and they establish only part of what you asked about.

On pricing and plans: Xero's pricing page says prices are in AUD and include GST, that Xero reserves the right to change pricing at any time, and that Xero subscriptions auto-renew monthly until cancelled (E3). In a section labelled "Grow", the page lists "$7.80 per month" then "$78 per month" (E3). Plans named on that page are Grow, Comprehensive and Ultimate 10 (E3). Xero says it offers several plans to suit different business sizes and needs and points to the pricing page to compare them and start a 30-day free trial (E5). There is also a promotion under which purchasing any Xero plan gives the first month free (E2, E6). The pricing page offers to point you to the right plan in under two minutes based on a few details about your business (E1). If you change to a less expensive plan, you can do so 1 month after upgrading (E3).

On features: the Grow listing says the plan includes "Smart document capture basic extraction", "Payroll for 2 people", "60 day cashflow forecast" and "Claim expenses and mileage for 1 user" (E3). The pricing page's comparison table also mentions items such as additional-user charges and per-bill-payment charges, but the extracted text does not make clear which plan each row belongs to. The accounting-software page says Xero is cloud-based, so you can log in wherever you have an internet connection, and that accounting software helps small business owners manage financial admin including tracking income and expenses, managing invoices, reconciling bank transactions and preparing financial reports (E5).

On payroll: the Grow listing includes "Payroll for 2 people" (E3), and Xero states it is ATO-certified for STP (E5). The pricing page notes that if you select a plan which includes Payroll, Expenses or Projects, additional charges may apply if you go over the stated included number of users (Expenses and Projects) or people paid (Payroll), and that invited users with access to those features may trigger additional charges if included usage or numbers are exceeded (E3).

On invoicing: the accounting-software page describes managing invoices as part of what the software does (E5), and a customer review on that page mentions appreciating the automated bank feeds, invoicing features and easy reconciliation process (E4). No invoicing-specific pricing or feature detail beyond this appears in the passages.

Beyond these points, the passages do not set out a complete price list, per-plan feature matrix, or payroll and invoicing detail, so much of your question is not established by the evidence.
cases.notes: All passages are from Xero's Australian site (region AU) and the pricing page states prices are in AUD and include GST; passages were retrieved on 2026-09-14. Pricing, plans and promotions are region- and time-specific, so these figures apply only to that region and retrieval date. Passage E4 consists of customer review text and E1/E2/E6 contain marketing copy; no instruction-like content was present, only promotional text.
unknowns: The full price and feature details of the Comprehensive and Ultimate 10 plans (only the plan names appear in E3).
Which plans the additional-user charges, per-bill-payment charges, budget counts and 60/90/180 day forecast rows in the E3 comparison table belong to.
Whether the "$7.80 per month" figure is an introductory or promotional rate, and its duration.
Payroll pricing details, such as the cost of paying more people than the included number, and payroll inclusions on plans other than the "Grow" listing.
Invoicing-specific pricing or feature details, beyond generic descriptions of managing invoices.
Pricing, plans and promotions outside the AU region and AUD currency, or as at any date other than the retrieval date.
